clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says there's a reason eating an orange works better than drinking the juice: the fiber in the whole fruit slows everything down.

His point: that slower pace lets more of the vitamin C and bioflavonoids get absorbed in the intestine instead of the stomach. Drink straight juice, he says, and more of it breaks down too fast in the stomach instead - which can even leave you with extra acid.

His line for it: animals in the wild don't have juice machines. Just saying.

Fruit or juice - which do you reach for first?

clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says to check your supplement label for two things that have nothing to do with the actual nutrient.

First: fillers, also called excipients, added to help manufacturing and shelf life, not your health.

Second: dyes. If a supplement lists any dye, red, blue or otherwise, his rule is simple: put it back on the shelf.

His harder rule: once you spot a dye on a label, don't buy anything else from that company either.
